PAN fabrics were coated with Ni–Co alloys at two weight ratios: Ni0.2Co0.8 and Ni0.8Co0.2.
Coating times varied from 0.5 minutes to 8 minutes to study effects on absorption.
XRD confirmed hcp Co phases for Ni0.2Co0.8 and fcc Ni–Co alloy phases for Ni0.8Co0.2 coatings.
SEM images showed nanoparticle clusters distributed on fabric fibers, with roughness increasing with coating time.
Electromagnetic constitutive parameters (ε', ε'', μ', μ'') were extracted using the Nicolson–Ross–Weir method from measured S-parameters.
Dielectric loss tangents (tan δ_e) were higher than magnetic loss tangents (tan δ_m), indicating dielectric-dominated absorption.
Return loss (RL) values reached below −20 dB over approximately 2 GHz bandwidth in X, Ku, and K bands for samples with shortest coating times.
Longer coating times led to cracked layers and reduced absorption performance.
The center frequency of minimum RL shifted depending on Ni/Co ratio: above 16 GHz for Ni0.2Co0.8 and below 16 GHz for Ni0.8Co0.2.
The coated fabrics had thicknesses around 2 mm during microwave testing.
The polymer overcoat prevented oxidation of Ni–Co nanoparticles.
The study used a vector network analyzer (Agilent PNA E8364B) with waveguide sample holders for microwave measurements.
The lattice constants for hcp Co phase were a=2.505 Å and c=4.09 Å, close to ideal values.
Crystals sizes calculated by Scherrer’s formula ranged from 13.76 nm to 23.43 nm for different crystal planes.
The microwave absorption bandwidth did not significantly change with coating time.
The electroless deposition process is low-cost, low-temperature (<100°C), and suitable for industrial scale.
The coated fabrics are flexible, lightweight, and thin, suitable for military radar camouflage applications.
The study confirms that tuning Ni/Co ratio and coating time allows optimization of RAM microwave absorption properties.
